tender.title: Terra Nova Construction Materials
tender.description:
An Open Framework to facilitate the supply of bulk construction materials to Terra Nova, Great Places Housing Group's in-house new build construction arm. Terra Nova intends that the Open Framework scheme of frameworks will endure for eight years, with annual iterations re-opening the Open Framework to competition, providing for potential new entrants, and that orders will be called off on a scheme by scheme basis, either with or without further competition. 
Initial Categories will include: Bulk Bricks, Bulk Blocks, Bulk First & Second Fix Joinery Timber

frameworkAgreement.description:
Contracts may be awarded to successful suppliers with a place on the framework either with or without competition, in compliance with §45 of PA23.
Any contracts under the framework awarded without competition will be awarded according to
objective mechanisms detailed in the Framework Agreement.
The process is detailed in the associated tender documents.

criteria.description:
Financial Capacity Conditions of Participation:
Financial Standing - Annual turnover must be at least twice the annual Lot value.
Lot 1 Bricks estimated annual turnover: £500,000
Insurance - Confirm willingness to obtain required insurance:
Employer’s (Compulsory) Liability Insurance* = [£5m]
Public Liability Insurance = [£5m]
Product Indemnity Insurance = [£5m]
Real Living Wage - Supplier must commit to pay in line with the Real Living Wage.
Legal Capacity Conditions of Participation:
Data Protection - Supplier must be willing to complete Data Protection Impact Assessment and confirm ICO compliance.
ICO Regulatory Action - Supplier must confirm whether their organisation has been subject to regulatory action.
Modern Slavery:  
Please advise us of the measures followed by your company to identify, prevent and mitigate risks of modern slavery within your organisation and throughout your supply chain for the materials proposed under this contract. 
1. If you are a relevant commercial organisation subject to Section 54 of the Modern Slavery Act 2015, that is, you carry on your business, or part of your business in the UK, supplying goods or services and you have an annual turnover of at least £36 million, please attach your current Modern Slavery statement, or a link to it.
OR
2. If you are not a relevant commercial organisation, but have a Modern Slavery Policy, please attach or link to that.
OR
3. Describe in up to 250 words what measures you take to:
•	Identify Modern Slavery risks
•	Mitigate & Prevent those risks
In all cases you response will be assessed for the adequacy of the measures described.

Sustainability:  
Please describe how you can assure Terra Nova of the measures you are taking to minimise waste and reduce carbon footprints throughout the supply chain
Deliveries:  
Suppliers must be able to deliver across Terra Nova sites as required
Delivery Timeframes:  
Suppliers to Lot 1 must be able to provide initial deliveries to a call-off contract within four weeks of the contract being agreed, and then provide subsequent deliveries to the schedule provided at call-off.  
All other orders must be delivered within two working days.
Credit Account Set-Up:  
Great Places must be able to set up a credit account with suppliers within a week of confirmation of call-off contracts
Cyber Security: 
Supplier must be willing to complete the Security Questionnaire and confirm resources to handle cyber security.

tender.riskDetails:
Supplier Performance Risks:
Supplier performance failure resulting in poor service levels, delayed deliveries, product quality
issues, or inadequate customer service.
Supply Chain Risks:
Supply chain disruption causing shortages of materials or delays in product availability.
Financial Stability Risks:
Supplier insolvency or business failure leading to interruptions in the provision of goods.
Pricing and Market Risks:
Price increases and market volatility affecting the cost of materials, transport, or distribution services.
Capacity and Demand Risks:
Demand exceeding supplier capacity, particularly in circumstances where the demand increases, for
instance, should GPHG merge with other organisations.
Quality, Health and Safety Risks:
Health & Safety, and product compliance failures resulting from goods not meeting required specifications, standards, or regulations, in particular for products falling under COSHH regulations.
Contract Management Risks:
Contract management resource constraints limiting effective supplier oversight and performance
monitoring.
Competition Risks:
Failure to maintain competition throughout the framework term due to supplier attrition or reduced
supplier participation within individual Lots.
Innovation Risks:
Lack of supplier innovation or continuous improvement over the life of the framework, resulting in missed opportunities for efficiencies, cost savings, or service enhancements.
Regulatory Risks:
Changes in industry standards, or legislative and regulatory requirements that impact the supply or
use of materials covered by the framework.
Sustainability Risks:
Environmental or sustainability performance risks where suppliers fail to meet agreed commitments
relating to responsible sourcing, carbon reduction or waste management.
Cyber Security and Data Protection Risks:
Cyber security or data protection incidents affecting suppliers, particularly given that electronic ordering,
invoicing, and inventory management systems are used.
